discovery: Invention and development of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori proposed in 2001 that neutral atoms could be trapped in an optical lattice at a 'magic wavelength', where the light shifts of both clock states cancel. This lets many atoms be interrogated at once without perturbing the transition. He demonstrated the first such clocks with strontium. Ye turned the concept into instruments of extraordinary stability and accuracy. He pushed systematic uncertainties toward the 10^-19 level, used spin-polarised degenerate Fermi gases to suppress collisional shifts, and resolved the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. This is measurement science at its best: by understanding and defeating every source of noise and systematic error, they produced a new tool for fundamental physics. It now tests general relativity at laboratory scales and searches for dark matter and for variation of the fundamental constants. It is also driving the redefinition of the SI second. The invention is decisive, mature and transformative.
